free.title: RAINY DAY IN BROOKLYN
free.caption:
RAINY DAY · BROOKLYN PUBLIC LIBRARY

Rain's not stopping today, so here's the free indoor spot most visitors skip: the Central branch of Brooklyn Public Library at Grand Army Plaza.

This Art Deco landmark opened in 1941 and still surprises people - a 50-foot bronze portico with fifteen literary figures carved into the entrance, then reading rooms big enough to lose an afternoon in. No ticket, no membership, no line. Open 9am to 8pm today.

Grab a table, bring a book (or borrow one off the open shelves), and let the storm do its thing outside the window.

If it clears up, the Grand Army Plaza greenmarket and 7th Ave shops are a five-minute walk away.

Save this for the next downpour and send it to whoever's stuck without plans today.

📷 Pexels

food.title: GRAY'S PAPAYA RECESSION SPECIAL
food.caption:
CHEAP EATS · GRAY'S PAPAYA

Two hot dogs and a drink for $7.50 - Gray's Papaya on the Upper West Side is still one of the last real cheap eats in Manhattan.

They call it the Recession Special: two all-beef hot dogs plus a medium tropical drink, tax included, at the counter on Broadway and 72nd. No seats, no menu to study - you order standing up like every regular before you.

Load it with mustard, kraut, and onions for free, and if you want to go big, the three-dog combo runs $11.50.

Open 8am to 10pm today, a half block from the 1/2/3 and B/C at 72nd St.

Save this for the next time someone says you can't eat in NYC for under $10.

📷 6sqft / David Joyce

art.title: 6 SECRETS OF GREEN-WOOD CEMETERY
art.caption:
HIDDEN GEM · GREEN-WOOD CEMETERY

Green-Wood Cemetery in Brooklyn opened in 1838, before Central Park existed, and it's still free to walk in - 478 acres of Gothic gates and hills most New Yorkers never explore.

By 1860 it was the second-biggest tourist draw in New York State, after Niagara Falls. The chapel was designed by Warren & Wetmore, the same firm behind Grand Central Terminal, and catacombs from the 1850s still sit underground, opened occasionally for tours.

Climb Battle Hill, Brooklyn's highest natural point, where a bronze Minerva statue faces the Statue of Liberty. Look up at the main gate for the wild monk parakeets nesting there since the 1970s.

Open daily, 7am to 7pm, always free.

Save this for your next free Brooklyn walk.

📷 Untapped New York
